analogs.covers: Almost everything: a big family pack around a breeding pair, strict ranks, pack territories and wars with rival packs
Courtship: suitors win mates with carefully chosen gifts and displays

headline: A Yellowstone-style wolf family pack around an alpha pair, at war with rival packs, where suitors court with bowerbird gifts.

setting.label: Pack territories in canyons, hills and forests
setting.note: Family packs claim large territories in their preferred POIs, either compact or grand. Solitary animals and bonded pairs are nomadic.

playsLike: You are a medium carnivore in a family pack around an alpha pair (up to 20 adults grouped in-game), with betas (their offspring) leading hunts and omegas filling the ranks. Every related member must share the pack's colour scheme or be exiled. Hunts use up to 5: circling, bluffing, running through groups to split out the weak. You take Large tier, or Apex only if nothing else is in sight. You are tolerant of other species but wage vicious territory wars against rival Utahraptor packs. Dispersers court at territory edges with gifts.

why.text: Packs are related individuals plus unrelated mates around one alpha pair. Real wolf packs are families around a breeding pair (official inspiration: canines).
Territories are defended only against other Utahraptor, and challenges can wipe out whole packs. Rival wolf packs fight exactly like this.
Circles prey, growls and snaps to intimidate, and runs through groups to separate the weak, the way wolves test a herd.
Young adults travel alone to the edges of other packs' territories to find a mate, as dispersing wolves do.
Suitors present gifts, and alphas may reject poor offerings. That is the bowerbird's game (official inspiration).

notLike: Wolf pups don't get exiled for their coat colour; Utahraptor packs enforce the alpha pair's colour scheme.
twist: Birds of prey (official inspiration) for its keen eyesight.
